title: Fit each month's work to the crews

blocks.text: The program manager sent the list to the crew supervisor, who answered:

Your list needs 45 crew-weeks of trimming. I have two crews from April to September, and I plan them a month at a time: each crew gives me four weeks a month. Tell me which circuits to trim *and in which month*, without ever booking more work in a month than my crews can do.

You start from the knapsack of the lesson before. Read each circuit's crew-weeks and the season's crews and months, and have the generator draw them. Let the model choose the month of each trimmed circuit, trim a circuit in one month at most, and keep each month's booked crew-weeks within what its crews can do, as well as the season within its budget. Keep anything HiGHS prints out of the report. The report shows each month's booked crew-weeks against its capacity. A season of one month is a season too: its crews may stop a trim the budget allows.

**The report.** The first line gains `, crews <crews>, months <months>`. After the status line comes one line per month, from month 1 to the last, an empty month included: two spaces, `month <m>: `, the crew-weeks booked that month right-aligned in two characters, `/`, the month's capacity and ` crew-weeks`; then, only when the month has trims, two spaces and the trims sorted by circuit id, each as `<cid>(<weeks>)`, one space apart. An empty month's line ends at `crew-weeks`, so no line ends in a space.

**Which months.** The objective counts the risk removed whatever the month, so the tiny season has several equally good plans, and the months HiGHS returns depend on the order the model is built in (the lesson shows the same model built in two orders giving two plans). `expected/report.txt` comes from this order: the variables circuit by circuit in the season's order, months 1 to the last within each circuit; then the once rows in circuit order, the crew rows in month order, the budget row, and the objective, solved with HiGHS at a relative gap of zero. Build yours in that order for the report check; the tests accept any order.

Run executes `main.py`, which plans the tiny season (six circuits of GridCap, a fictional utility, drawn by `vegcrew/generate.py` from seed 54) and prints the report; `expected/report.txt` is the report it should print. Submit runs every test in `tests/`, the earlier steps' included, and compares Run's report with the expected one.
Write each method below. The tests check each one by itself and the whole program end to end, so you may change any other part of the code as you see fit.
def build(season: Season) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict[tuple[str, int], mathopt.Variable]]

items: **Contract.** Takes a Season. Returns a MathOpt model and one binary x[(cid, m)] per circuit and month m from 1 to season.months (named `x_<cid>_<m>`): a row `once_<cid>` per circuit (trimmed in at most one month), a row `crews_<m>` per month (the crew-weeks of the circuits trimmed that month within crews times WEEKS_PER_MONTH), a row budget, and the summed risk of the trimmed circuits as the objective to maximize. The expected report comes from this build order: the variables circuit by circuit in the season's order, months 1 to season.months within each circuit; then the once rows in circuit order, the crews rows in month order, the budget row, and the objective. The objective does not name the month, so another order can give other months that are just as good; the tests accept them, the report check does not.
**Modeling idea.** A start-month binary per circuit and month carries the when; each month's crews are one more capacity row, and the once row keeps a circuit from being counted twice.

**Taught in** [6.4.1 Start-Time Variables x[i,t] and Timing Windows](../../../../06-formulation-craft/26-multi-period-timing/units/unit-01/6.4.1-start-time-variables-x-i-t-and-timing-windows.unit.html).
**Contract.** Solves the model with HiGHS at a relative gap of zero and returns the SolveResult, with nothing HiGHS writes at the C level reaching the program's standard output.
**Modeling idea.** The HiGHS bundled with OR-Tools can print a stray debug line on some MIP solves; the report a manager reads must not carry it.
**Taught in** [14.1.2 Crews and Months: Capacity Over Time](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/54-project-vegetation-crews/units/unit-02/14.1.2-crews-and-months-capacity-over-time.unit.html).
**Contract.** Builds and quietly solves the model, and returns a Plan with one Trim(cid, month) per variable above 0.5, and the trimmed circuits' summed cost and risk removed.
**Modeling idea.** The schedule is read off the variables that are 1; the key of each variable says the month.

**Taught in** [6.4.1 Start-Time Variables x[i,t] and Timing Windows](../../../../06-formulation-craft/26-multi-period-timing/units/unit-01/6.4.1-start-time-variables-x-i-t-and-timing-windows.unit.html).
**Contract.** Also reads each circuit's weeks (crew-weeks to trim it) and the season's crews and months; columns the planner does not use are still ignored.
**Modeling idea.** Read the columns the model needs now, and only those.
**Taught in** [14.1.2 Crews and Months: Capacity Over Time](../../../../14-growing-real-projects/54-project-vegetation-crews/units/unit-02/14.1.2-crews-and-months-capacity-over-time.unit.html).

"""Turn a season into a plan: which circuits to trim, and in which month, solved by HiGHS through MathOpt."""

from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import os
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt

from vegcrew.data import WEEKS_PER_MONTH, Season

EXACT = mathopt.SolveParameters(relative_gap_tolerance=0.0)
STATUS = {mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL: "OPTIMAL", mathopt.TerminationReason.FEASIBLE: "FEASIBLE",
          mathopt.TerminationReason.INFEASIBLE: "INFEASIBLE"}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Trim:
    cid: str
    month: int                                      # 1 to season.months
    crew: str = ""                                  # stub for lesson 14.1.3
    start: int = 0                                  # stub for lesson 14.1.3
    end: int = 0                                    # stub for lesson 14.1.3


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:
    status: str                                     # OPTIMAL, FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE or NOT_SOLVED
    trims: dict[str, Trim] = field(default_factory=dict)
    cost: int = 0                                   # $k spent
    risk_removed: int = 0                           # $k a year of risk the trims remove


def crew_ids(season: Season) -> list[str]:
    """Stub for lesson 14.1.3."""
    return []


def horizon(season: Season) -> int:
    """Stub for lesson 14.1.3."""
    return 0


def build(season: Season) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict[tuple[str, int], mathopt.Variable]]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name=f"trim_{season.name}")
    months = range(1, season.months + 1)
    x = {(c.cid, m): model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{c.cid}_{m}") for c in season.circuits for m in months}

    def trimmed(cid: str) -> mathopt.LinearExpression:
        return mathopt.fast_sum(x[cid, m] for m in months)

    for c in season.circuits:
        model.add_linear_constraint(trimmed(c.cid) <= 1, name=f"once_{c.cid}")
    for m in months:
        model.add_linear_constraint(
            mathopt.fast_sum(c.weeks * x[c.cid, m] for c in season.circuits) <= season.crews * WEEKS_PER_MONTH,
            name=f"crews_{m}")
    model.add_linear_constraint(mathopt.fast_sum(c.cost * trimmed(c.cid) for c in season.circuits) <= season.budget,
                                name="budget")
    model.maximize(mathopt.fast_sum(c.risk * trimmed(c.cid) for c in season.circuits))
    return model, x


def solve_quietly(model: mathopt.Model) -> mathopt.SolveResult:
    """Solve with HiGHS, keeping its stray C-level debug line off the program's standard output.

    The HiGHS bundled in OR-Tools 9.15 prints `HighsMipSolverData::transformNewIntegerFeasibleSolution`
    on some MIP solves even with no log asked for, and only when the process exits. Standard output
    points at /dev/null for the solve, and the C buffer is flushed there before it is restored.
    """
    sys.stdout.flush()
    saved, sink = os.dup(1), os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY)
    os.dup2(sink, 1)
    try:
        return mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS, params=EXACT)
    finally:
        ctypes.CDLL(None).fflush(None)
        os.dup2(saved, 1)
        os.close(saved)
        os.close(sink)


def make_plan(season: Season) -> Plan:
    """Choose the circuits to trim and their months: the most risk removed within the budget and the crews."""
    model, x = build(season)
    result = solve_quietly(model)
    status = STATUS.get(result.termination.reason, result.termination.reason.name)
    if status not in ("OPTIMAL", "FEASIBLE"):
        return Plan(status)
    trims = {cid: Trim(cid, m) for (cid, m), v in x.items() if result.variable_values(v) > 0.5}
    chosen = [season.circuit(cid) for cid in trims]
    return Plan(status, trims, cost=sum(c.cost for c in chosen), risk_removed=sum(c.risk for c in chosen))

"""GridCap's vegetation crew planner.

GridCap is a fictional utility, and every season this package plans is generated from a seed by
`vegcrew.generate`. None of it is a real utility's data.
"""

"""python -m vegcrew [tiny|small|medium] [--seed N]: plan a generated season and print the plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from vegcrew.data import season_from_dict
from vegcrew.generate import SIZES, scenario
from vegcrew.planner import make_plan
from vegcrew.report import format_plan


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="vegcrew")
    parser.add_argument("size", nargs="?", default="small", choices=sorted(SIZES))
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=54)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    season = season_from_dict(scenario(args.size, args.seed))
    print(format_plan(season, make_plan(season)))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""The plan as the vegetation manager reads it."""

from __future__ import annotations

from vegcrew.data import WEEKS_PER_MONTH, Season
from vegcrew.planner import Plan


def format_plan(season: Season, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"season {season.name}: {len(season.circuits)} circuits, budget ${season.budget:,}k, "
             f"crews {season.crews}, months {season.months}",
             f"status {plan.status}: {len(plan.trims)} trims, cost ${plan.cost:,}k, "
             f"risk removed ${plan.risk_removed:,}k a year"]
    for m in range(1, season.months + 1):
        cids = sorted(cid for cid, t in plan.trims.items() if t.month == m)
        used = sum(season.circuit(cid).weeks for cid in cids)
        work = " ".join(f"{cid}({season.circuit(cid).weeks})" for cid in cids)
        lines.append(f"  month {m}: {used:>2}/{season.crews * WEEKS_PER_MONTH} crew-weeks  {work}".rstrip())
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""python -m vegcrew [tiny|small|medium] [--seed N]: plan a generated season and print the plan."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse

from vegcrew.data import season_from_dict
from vegcrew.generate import SIZES, scenario

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="vegcrew")
    parser.add_argument("size", nargs="?", default="small", choices=sorted(SIZES))
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=54)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    season = season_from_dict(scenario(args.size, args.seed))

"""The plan as the vegetation manager reads it."""

from __future__ import annotations

from vegcrew.data import Season
from vegcrew.planner import Plan


def format_plan(season: Season, plan: Plan) -> str:
    lines = [f"season {season.name}: {len(season.circuits)} circuits, budget ${season.budget:,}k",
             f"status {plan.status}: {len(plan.trims)} trims, cost ${plan.cost:,}k, "
             f"risk removed ${plan.risk_removed:,}k a year"]
    for cid in sorted(plan.trims):
        c = season.circuit(cid)
        lines.append(f"  {cid} {c.region:<5} {c.miles:>3} mi  cost ${c.cost:>4}k  risk ${c.risk:>4}k")
    return "\n".join(lines)
